title: Headings Qualified by Nationality, Ethnic Group, Language, etc.
summary: Each heading with an adjectival qualifier for nationality, ethnic group, language, etc. must be individually established, except that inverted subdivisions with adjectival qualifiers may take any adjective when a multiple subdivision exists. Qualified headings are inverted, except those for U.S. ethnic groups, Indian groups, major literary forms, religious adjectives, and a few other established patterns. References run from the alternate (straight/inverted) form; subdivision reference structures are not duplicated under qualified headings.
validation_rules: A heading with an adjectival qualifier for nationality, ethnic group, language, etc. is valid only if that specific qualified heading is established (e.g. `Investments, American`, `Art, American`, `Mythology, Armenian`, `Short stories, English`, `Mexican American children`); the existence of the unqualified heading does not authorize arbitrary qualification. (H 320 sec. 1)

Exception: an inverted subdivision with an adjectival qualifier may take any appropriate adjective without individual establishment when a multiple subdivision exists in the authority file or on a free-floating list, e.g. `World War, 1939-1945--Personal narratives, American`; `United States--Foreign public opinion, British`. (H 320 sec. 1; H 1090)

An uninverted subdivision with an adjectival qualifier (e.g. `--American influences`) for which no multiple exists must be individually established under each heading, e.g. `France--Civilization--American influences`. (H 320 sec. 1)
Qualified headings are inverted: `[Heading], [Adjective]` (e.g. `Art, French`, `College and school drama, French`). (H 320 sec. 2)

Exceptions in uninverted (direct) form: headings qualified by ethnic groups of the United States or by Indian groups (`African American children`, `Mexican American art`); major literary forms (H 306 sec. 2.a.(1), H 351) (`English poetry`, `French drama`); a few other well-established patterns (`French students`, `Indian women`, `American property`, `German imprints`); and headings with adjectives for religious groups including `Jewish` and `Islamic`. (H 320 sec. 2)

The alternate-order form of a qualified heading is a UF reference, not a valid heading: `French art` (for `Art, French`), `Art, Mexican American` (for `Mexican American art`), `French college and school drama` (for `College and school drama, French`). (H 320 sec. 3)
Use only the established form of a national or ethnic adjective; non-used variant adjectival forms are handled by general see references (H 374) and are invalid in headings. (H 320 sec. 3)

A subdivision established under the unqualified heading may also appear under the qualified heading, e.g. `Corporations--Investor relations` and `Corporations, American--Investor relations`. (H 320 sec. 4)

sections.heading: 1. General provision.
sections.text:
Establish editorially each instance of a subject heading with an adjectival qualifier for nationality, ethnic group, language, etc. Examples:

```
150 ## $a Investments, American
150 ## $a Art, American
150 ## $a Mythology, Armenian
150 ## $a Short stories, English
150 ## $a Mexican American children
```

Exception: In the case of inverted subdivisions with adjectival qualifiers, individual adjectives may be applied without establishing each usage if a multiple subdivision has been provided in the subject authority file or on a free-floating list. For instructions on multiple subdivisions, see H 1090. Examples:

```
650 #0 $a World War, 1939-1945 $v Personal narratives, American.
651 #0 $a United States $x Foreign public opinion, British.
```

If the subdivision is uninverted and no multiple has been provided, establish each instance as needed. Example:

```
151 ## $a France $x Civilization $x American influences.
```

sections.heading: 2. Inverted or uninverted headings.
sections.text:
Establish all qualified headings in the inverted form except for those qualified by ethnic groups of the United States or by Indian groups, major literary forms (see H 306, sec. 2.a.(1); H 351), and a few other well-established patterns.

Note: Headings qualified by adjectives for religious groups, including the adjectives Jewish and Islamic, are established in uninverted form (cf. H 306, sec. 1).

Examples:

```
150 ## $a English poetry
150 ## $a African American children
150 ## $a French students
150 ## $a Indian women
150 ## $a American property
150 ## $a German imprints
```

sections.heading: 3. References.
sections.text:
Add as a standard reference to a qualified heading of this type a 450 field with the alternative form of the heading. If the heading is inverted, make the reference from the straight form; if straight, make the reference from the inverted form. Examples:

```
150 ## $a Art, French
450 ## $a French art

150 ## $a Mexican American art
450 ## $a Art, Mexican American
```

Do not add references from non-used variant forms of national and ethnic adjectival qualifiers. Instead make general see references from non-used adjectival variants according to the procedures in H 374.

Add additional 4XX or 5XX fields as appropriate. Example:

```
150 ## $a College and school drama, French
450 ## $a French college and school drama
550 ## $w g $a French drama
```

sections.heading: 4. References for subdivisions used under qualified headings.
sections.text:
When a subdivision established under the unqualified form of a heading has been provided with a complete reference structure, that reference structure should not normally be duplicated if the same subdivision is established under the qualified heading. Examples:

```
150 ## $a Corporations $x Investor relations
[unqualified heading with subdivision]
450 ## $a Investor relations (Corporations)
550 ## $w g $a Public relations $x Corporations
550 ## $w g $a Stockholders

150 ## $a Corporations, American $x Investor relations
[qualified heading with subdivision; no additional references needed]
```
